description: Post-run private-root inventory, workspace snapshot, symlink checks, and path-specific preflight repairs

description: bench(cache): establish clean-client remote baseline

asi.evidence: After an outlier run under system load, the stable repeat measured 173.55 ms median versus the 176.89 ms baseline. Two earlier repeats of the same fast path measured 174.85 and 175.03 ms.

asi.next: Move validated host tool identity caching out of disposable workspace action state, then optimize prelude selection.

description: perf(cache): reuse remote session initialization

asi.evidence: Two controlled remote runs measured 143.42 and 148.71 ms median versus the 176.89 ms baseline. The stable repeat improved median latency by 15.9 percent.
asi.hypothesis: Host executable paths and safe version probes are machine identity, not disposable action state. Retaining them avoids toolchain-manager and Node process startup after an action-cache clear.
asi.next: Replace the full prelude source scan with indexed target-kind metadata and return to local-hit measurement.

description: perf(toolchain): retain validated host identity across cache clears

asi.evidence: The indexed selector measured 23.95 ms median over 40 local hits versus the preceding system-allocator result of 25.13 ms. Focused tests and strict frontend lint pass.

asi.next: Measure evidence-store synchronization and remaining per-target blocking-pool handoffs.

description: perf(frontend): index built-in target kind modules

asi.evidence: The shortcut measured 24.37 ms median, while the immediate reverted baseline measured 23.53 ms with 0.85 ms standard deviation. The shortcut adds compatibility state without a measurable win.

description: Schema-version shortcut did not improve warmed evidence writes

asi.evidence: The stable 20-run median fell from 148.71 ms to 41.57 ms, a 72.0 percent reduction. Seventy-six content-store tests and strict linting passed. Incompressible local writes also borrow their source bytes, and streamed remote reads reserve bounded capacity.
asi.hypothesis: Remote action results are recoverable cache mirrors, so atomic visibility is sufficient and file plus directory durability synchronization is unnecessary on every clean-client hit.
asi.next: Overlap evidence database initialization with graph execution, then rerun the full cross-client benchmark.

description: perf(cache): avoid durable synchronization for remote mirrors

asi.evidence: Trace timestamps confirmed setup completed before graph execution and reduced the post-build tail to about 1.7 ms, but the 40-run median was 23.80 ms versus the immediate 23.53 ms control. Early SQLite worker creation delayed the frontend enough to erase the overlap.
asi.hypothesis: Starting the evidence connection alongside graph loading would hide database setup behind analysis and cache lookup.
asi.next: Keep evidence sequencing simple and target benchmark wrapper cost or action lookup dependencies instead.

description: Evidence initialization overlap moved rather than removed worker cost

asi.evidence: A 60-run comparison measured the process version floor at 4.35 ms median and the local hit at 21.77 ms median, leaving about 17 ms of actionable work.
asi.hypothesis: Eager remote client construction contributes to every local hit even when no remote request is made.
asi.next: Wrap remote client construction in a single-flight lazy cell and repeat the 40-run local benchmark.

description: Baseline before lazy remote client

asi.evidence: Two 40-run repeats measured 18.89 ms and 18.37 ms median versus the 22.02 ms baseline, improving the stable repeat by 16.6 percent. Focused tests and formatting checks passed.
asi.hypothesis: A local action-cache hit should not construct the unused remote Hypertext Transfer Protocol client and transport security state.
asi.next: Re-measure clean-client remote hits to confirm moving initialization does not regress the remote path, then profile duplicate manifest and module parsing.

description: perf(cache): defer remote client initialization

asi.evidence: The 40-run median regressed to 19.65 ms versus the 18.37 ms lazy-client baseline. The reversible setting does not justify a weaker crash-loss window.
asi.hypothesis: Reducing reconstructible workspace-database synchronization from FULL to NORMAL might remove commit tail latency without changing journal format.
asi.next: Retain full synchronization and avoid persistent write-ahead logging until a dedicated filesystem-compatibility design can justify it. Profile duplicate manifest reads or filesystem task handoffs next.

description: Reduced database synchronization did not improve local hits

name: Reduce remote blob mirror durability barriers

asi.evidence: The preceding 20-run clean-client benchmark measured 38.78 ms median after lazy remote-client initialization.
asi.hypothesis: A synchronized remote blob mirror pays one unnecessary parent-directory durability barrier on every clean-client output restoration.
asi.next: Restore the treatment that synchronizes blob contents but not the recoverable directory entry, then repeat with 30 clean-client runs.

description: Baseline before recoverable remote blob mirrors

asi.evidence: Two 30-run clean-client treatments measured 37.77 ms and 36.27 ms median versus the 39.99 ms control, a stable-repeat reduction of 9.3 percent. The path now rejects digest mismatches before writing, and focused content-store tests passed.
asi.hypothesis: Remote blob contents need synchronization before atomic rename, but their recoverable directory entry does not need a parent-directory durability barrier.
asi.next: Keep locally produced blobs fully durable. Update the cross-client report after full validation, then investigate manifest-read deduplication separately because it affects a narrower workspace shape.

description: perf(cache): retain durable contents for remote blob mirrors

asi.evidence: Five warmed local runs measured 23.10 to 23.54 MB maximum resident memory, while five version-only runs measured about 10.16 to 10.21 MB. The requested output is 1 MiB.
asi.hypothesis: Validating one requested file currently holds its raw bytes and encoded file-blob bytes simultaneously, adding about 2.1 MB of peak live memory and one full-file copy.
asi.next: Hash the file-blob prefix and file reader incrementally, prove digest identity against the existing encoded bytes, then repeat latency and resident-memory measurements.

description: Baseline before streaming file-blob validation

asi.evidence: The preceding baseline was 27.88 ms versus the established 18 to 20 ms range.
asi.hypothesis: The first segment baseline was inflated by transient host load and should not be used to judge a sub-millisecond content-hashing change.
asi.next: Use this immediate repeat as the latency control and preserve the separately sampled 23.1 to 23.5 MB resident-memory range.

description: Stable baseline before streaming file-blob validation

asi.evidence: Nine warmed treatment samples measured 21.61 MB median maximum resident memory versus 23.17 MB across the five-sample control, a 1.56 MB or 6.7 percent reduction. The stable 40-run latency repeat measured 19.21 ms versus the immediate 22.52 ms control. Exact digest-identity tests cover empty, one-byte, and one-megabyte files.
asi.hypothesis: Hashing the file-blob prefix and file contents incrementally removes the second one-megabyte buffer and full-file copy from every unchanged requested output.
asi.next: Share the measured result with Claude, then reduce immutable AnalysisEngine deep clones for representative large workspaces.

description: perf(outputs): stream cached file validation

asi.evidence: The 15-target fixture has one target kind and should expose only about 75 avoidable allocations; a 500-target workspace with 60 kinds would perform about 64,000 avoidable allocations.
asi.hypothesis: Immutable callback metadata, options, and configuration are deep-cloned for each target task even though only the host cache requires shared mutation.
asi.next: Restore the shared-ownership treatment and require no regression on the small fixture plus cloned-engine isolation tests.

description: Baseline before shared analysis metadata

asi.evidence: Two 40-run treatments measured 24.96 ms and 28.48 ms median versus the 22.65 ms control. The fixture performs only about 75 avoided allocations, and the changed ownership layout consistently lost despite focused correctness tests passing.
asi.hypothesis: Sharing immutable callback metadata, analysis options, and configuration would replace per-target deep clones with cheap reference-count increments.
asi.next: Keep the existing owned engine fields. Reapply only exact String capacity reservation, then focus on repeated manifest and module loading with direct measurements.

description: Shared analysis metadata regressed the local fixture

asi.evidence: Nine one-mebibyte cold-materialization samples measured 27,836,416 bytes median maximum resident memory versus 27,852,800 bytes across seven control samples. Resident memory is flat because allocator pages from cache fetch are reused, but source inspection confirms the second full output allocation and copy are removed. All 168 core unit tests, five integration tests, strict linting, and formatting passed.
asi.hypothesis: Restoring a prefetched file from its staging path should stream through a fixed-size copy buffer instead of allocating another full blob Vec.
asi.next: Prune workspace traversal using safe literal include roots, which should avoid entry allocations and filesystem calls for unrelated trees.

description: perf(outputs): stream staged file materialization

asi.evidence: The 40-run warmed local control measured 20.44 milliseconds median. The benchmark manifest includes only the root once.toml, but the current walker still enters every non-hidden directory.
asi.hypothesis: A workspace with literal include roots should not walk unrelated top-level directory trees.
asi.next: Derive only provably literal top-level include roots and use them to prune WalkDir without changing wildcard behavior.

description: Baseline before include-root pruning

asi.evidence: Using the same release executable and a temporary 5,000-branch unrelated tree, 40 runs measured 11.36 milliseconds median with literal-root pruning versus 127.61 milliseconds with an equivalent wildcard include that forces traversal, a 91.1 percent reduction. Wildcard patterns retain full traversal. Focused tests, strict linting, and formatting passed.
asi.hypothesis: Workspace traversal can safely prune top-level directories when every include pattern has a literal first component.
asi.next: Reserve exact capacity for combined Starlark source and then run the full validation suite.

description: perf(frontend): prune literal workspace include roots

asi.evidence: The no-module path is proven borrowed by a focused test. The custom-module 40-run repeat measured 22.61 milliseconds versus 22.51 milliseconds immediately before this treatment, effectively flat under current host noise. Module tests, strict linting, and formatting passed.
asi.hypothesis: Clone-on-write module composition can remove the temporary built-in source copy when no custom modules exist, while exact capacity avoids repeated growth when files are appended.
asi.next: Run complete workspace validation, update the benchmark report with resident-memory and traversal results, and ask Claude to challenge the retained design.

description: perf(frontend): borrow unchanged module source

asi.evidence: Two 40-run treatments measured 20.69 and 19.05 milliseconds median versus the preceding 22.61-millisecond repeat. The stable treatment is 15.7 percent lower. The source now reserves the exact selected prelude size, borrows index path strings, and reuses the first output metadata lookup. Focused tests, strict linting, formatting, full workspace tests, and 241 command-line specifications passed.
asi.hypothesis: The graph-build path knows all selected prelude lengths in advance and can avoid repeated String growth plus cloned static path names.
asi.next: Retain bounded portable I/O. Design remote stream-to-cache as a separate change before replacing capture buffering, because generic put_stream intentionally limits very large remote uploads today.

description: perf(frontend): pre-size selected module source
